nodes.name: Galvin's theorem
nodes.statement: Let $\mathscr{F}$ be a normal filter over $\kappa$, where $\kappa$ is strongly regular and uncountable.\footnote{A cardinal $\kappa$ is \emph{strongly regular} if and only if $\kappa=\kappa^{<\kappa}$.} Galvin proved that every family $\mathcal{C}=\{C_\alpha:\alpha\in\kappa^+\}\subseteq\mathscr{F}$ admits a subfamily $\mathcal{D}=\{C_{\alpha_i}:i\in\kappa\}$ so that $\bigcap\mathcal{D}\in\mathscr{F}$, see \cite{MR0369081}.
nodes.statement_short: For a normal filter over a strongly regular uncountable $\kappa$, every $\kappa^+$-family from the filter has a $\kappa$-subfamily whose intersection is in the filter.

nodes.name: Galvin property ${\rm Gal}(\mathscr{F},\partial,\lambda)$
nodes.statement: Given $\aleph_0<\kappa\leq\partial\leq\lambda$ and a normal filter $\mathscr{F}$ over $\kappa$ let us write ${\rm Gal}(\mathscr{F},\partial,\lambda)$ to denote the statement that every $\mathcal{C}\subseteq\mathscr{F}$ of size $\lambda$ admits a subfamily $\mathcal{D}\subseteq\mathcal{C}$ of size $\partial$ such that $\bigcap\mathcal{D}\in\mathscr{F}$.
differentia: every $\mathcal{C}\subseteq\mathscr{F}$ of size $\lambda$ admits a subfamily $\mathcal{D}\subseteq\mathcal{C}$ of size $\partial$ such that $\bigcap\mathcal{D}\in\mathscr{F}$
nodes.statement_short: Gal(F, ∂, λ): every λ-sized subfamily of the filter F has a ∂-sized subfamily whose intersection lies in F.

nodes.name: Galvin's theorem (club filter of $\aleph_1$)
nodes.statement: Using this terminology, Galvin's theorem says that if $2^\omega=\omega_1$ then ${\rm Gal}(\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1},\aleph_1,\aleph_2)$ holds, where $\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1}$ is the club filter of $\aleph_1$.

nodes.name: Abraham-Shelah theorem (failure of the Galvin property)
nodes.statement: Abraham and Shelah proved in \cite{MR830084} that one can force $2^{\omega_1}=\lambda$ along with $\neg{\rm Gal}(\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1},\aleph_1,\lambda)$, where $\lambda$ is arbitrarily large.

nodes.name: Galvin property above the continuum
nodes.statement: It was shown in \cite{MR3604115} that this fact is not just a coincidence. To wit, if $\mu=(2^\omega)^+$ then ${\rm Gal}(\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1},\aleph_1,\mu)$ holds.
nodes.statement_short: If $\mu=(2^\omega)^+$ then the Galvin property ${\rm Gal}(\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1},\aleph_1,\mu)$ holds.

nodes.name: Monotonicity of the Galvin property in $\lambda$
nodes.statement: From the definition it follows that if $\mu'\geq\mu$ then ${\rm Gal}(\mathscr{F},\partial,\mu)$ implies ${\rm Gal}(\mathscr{F},\partial,\mu')$.

nodes.name: Galvin property when the continuum is small
nodes.statement: Thus, if $2^\omega<\lambda$ then ${\rm Gal}(\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1},\aleph_1,\lambda)$ follows.

nodes.name: The Galvin number $\mathfrak{gp}$
nodes.statement: The Galvin number. \newline Let $\mathfrak{gp}$ be the minimal $\kappa$ such that every family $\mathcal{C}=\{C_\alpha:\alpha\in\kappa^+\}$ of clubs of $\aleph_1$ contains a subfamily $\mathcal{D}=\{C_{\alpha_i}:i\in\omega_1\}$ so that $\bigcap\mathcal{D}\in\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1}$.
differentia: every family $\mathcal{C}=\{C_\alpha:\alpha\in\kappa^+\}$ of clubs of $\aleph_1$ contains a subfamily $\mathcal{D}=\{C_{\alpha_i}:i\in\omega_1\}$ so that $\bigcap\mathcal{D}\in\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1}$
nodes.statement_short: $\mathfrak{gp}$ is the least $\kappa$ such that every $\kappa^+$ clubs of $\aleph_1$ contain $\aleph_1$ many with club intersection.
nodes.label: defgp

nodes.name: Values of $\mathfrak{gp}$ in the Abraham-Shelah model
nodes.statement: In the model of Abraham and Shelah, one begins with an infinite cardinal $\lambda$ and forces $2^\omega=2^{\omega_1}=\lambda$ along with the failure of ${\rm Gal}(\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1},\aleph_1,\lambda)$. Observe that ${\rm Gal}(\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1},\aleph_1,(2^{\aleph_1})^+)$ is trivial, so ${\rm Gal}(\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1},\aleph_1,\lambda^+)$ holds in this setting. Consequently, $\mathfrak{gp}=\lambda$ in this model. This forcing construction applies to every $\lambda$ so that ${\rm cf}(\lambda)>\aleph_1$, hence $\mathfrak{gp}$ can be either regular or singular of cofinality above $\aleph_1$, at every $\lambda$ in the $\aleph$-scale.
nodes.statement_short: In the Abraham-Shelah model $\mathfrak{gp}=\lambda$, so $\mathfrak{gp}$ can be regular or singular of cofinality above $\aleph_1$.

nodes.name: Consistency of countable cofinality of $\mathfrak{gp}$
nodes.statement: In particular, it was asked in \cite[Question 4.4]{MR3787522} whether ${\rm cf}(\mathfrak{gp})=\omega$ is consistent.

nodes.name: Consistency strength of ${\rm cf}(\mathfrak{gp})=\omega$
nodes.statement: Though the question is still open, we know from \cite{MR4423479} that if ${\rm cf}(\mathfrak{gp})=\omega$ is consistent then it has some consistency strength.

nodes.name: Club filter $\mathscr{D}_\kappa$
nodes.statement: We denote the club filter over $\kappa$ by $\mathscr{D}_\kappa$ whenever $\kappa$ is regular and uncountable.

nodes.name: $\omega$-closed unbounded sets $\mathscr{U}^\kappa_\omega$
nodes.statement: The collection of $\omega$-closed unbounded subsets of $\kappa$ is denoted by $\mathscr{U}^\kappa_\omega$.

nodes.name: $\Theta$
nodes.statement: We let $\Theta$ be the supremum of $\lambda$ for which there is a surjection $\pi:{}^\omega\omega\rightarrow\lambda$.

nodes.name: Polarized partition relation
nodes.statement: Ahead of our first claim, recall that $\binom{\alpha}{\beta}\rightarrow\binom{\gamma}{\delta}$ denotes the statement that for every coloring $c:\alpha\times\beta\rightarrow\{0,1\}$ one can find $A\in[\alpha]^\gamma,B\in[\beta]^\delta$ so that $c\upharpoonright(A\times{B})$ is constant.
differentia: for every coloring $c:\alpha\times\beta\rightarrow\{0,1\}$ one can find $A\in[\alpha]^\gamma,B\in[\beta]^\delta$ so that $c\upharpoonright(A\times{B})$ is constant
nodes.statement_short: The polarized relation: every 2-coloring of $\alpha\times\beta$ has a monochromatic product of sizes $\gamma,\delta$.

nodes.name: Polarized relation with filter-sized sets
nodes.statement: One can replace the ordinals in this relation by some structure, with the natural intended meaning. Thus, if $\mathscr{W}\subseteq\mathcal{P}(\lambda)$ and $\mathscr{U}\subseteq\mathcal{P}(\kappa)$ then $\binom{\lambda}{\kappa}\rightarrow\binom{\mathscr{W}}{\mathscr{U}}$ means that the sets $A,B$ which form the monochromatic product belong to $\mathscr{W}$ and $\mathscr{U}$ respectively.
differentia: the sets $A,B$ which form the monochromatic product belong to $\mathscr{W}$ and $\mathscr{U}$ respectively

nodes.name: Full Galvin property at measurables
nodes.statement: Suppose that $\aleph_0<\kappa<\lambda$ and both $\kappa$ and $\lambda$ are measurable. Then ${\rm Gal}(\mathscr{U},\lambda,\lambda)$ holds whenever $\mathscr{U}$ is a normal ultrafilter over $\kappa$.
nodes.statement_short: If $\kappa<\lambda$ are measurable, every normal ultrafilter $\mathscr{U}$ on $\kappa$ satisfies ${\rm Gal}(\mathscr{U},\lambda,\lambda)$ (no choice needed).
nodes.label: clmmeasurables

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 2.1
nodes.statement: Let $\mathscr{U}$ be a normal ultrafilter over $\kappa$, and let $\mathscr{W}$ be a normal ultrafilter over $\lambda$. As a first step we prove the combinatorial relation $\binom{\lambda}{\kappa}\rightarrow\binom{\mathscr{W}}{\mathscr{U}}$. Then we derive the statement of the claim from this relation. Assume, therefore, that $c:\lambda\times\kappa\rightarrow{2}$ is given. For every $\beta\in\kappa$ there is a unique $j_\beta\in\{0,1\}$ for which $S^{j_\beta}_\beta=\{\alpha\in\lambda:c(\alpha,\beta)=j_\beta\}$ belongs to $\mathscr{W}$. It follows that for some fixed $j$ and a set $B\in\mathscr{U}$ one has $j_\beta=j$ whenever $\beta\in{B}$. Define $A=\bigcap\{S^j_\beta:\beta\in{B}\}$ and notice that $A\in\mathscr{W}$ by $\lambda$-completeness. Observe that $c''(A\times{B})=\{j\}$, hence we are done proving that $\binom{\lambda}{\kappa}\rightarrow\binom{\mathscr{W}}{\mathscr{U}}$. Assume now that $\{C_\alpha:\alpha\in\lambda\}\subseteq\mathscr{U}$. Define $d:\lambda\times\kappa\rightarrow{2}$ by letting $d(\alpha,\beta)=0$ iff $\beta\in{C_\alpha}$. Let $A\in\mathscr{W},B\in\mathscr{U}$ be such that $d\upharpoonright(A\times{B})$ is constant. Notice that the constant value cannot be $1$. Indeed, choose $\alpha\in{A}$ and any element $\beta\in B\cap C_\alpha$ and conclude that $\beta\notin C_\alpha$ if $d''(A\times{B})=\{1\}$, contradicting the choice of $\beta$. Thus $d''(A\times{B})=\{0\}$, and hence $B\subseteq\bigcap\{C_\alpha:\alpha\in{A}\}$. Since $B\in\mathscr{U}$, the proof is accomplished.
nodes.statement_short: First prove the polarized relation $\binom{\lambda}{\kappa}\rightarrow\binom{\mathscr{W}}{\mathscr{U}}$ via ultrafilter completeness, then apply it to the coloring $d(\alpha,\beta)=0$ iff $\beta\in C_\alpha$.

nodes.name: Fix ultrafilters and plan
nodes.statement: Let $\mathscr{U}$ be a normal ultrafilter over $\kappa$, and let $\mathscr{W}$ be a normal ultrafilter over $\lambda$. As a first step we prove the combinatorial relation $\binom{\lambda}{\kappa}\rightarrow\binom{\mathscr{W}}{\mathscr{U}}$. Then we derive the statement of the claim from this relation.
nodes.statement_short: Fix normal ultrafilters on $\kappa$, $\lambda$; plan: prove the polarized relation, then derive the claim.

nodes.name: Colors per column
nodes.statement: Assume, therefore, that $c:\lambda\times\kappa\rightarrow{2}$ is given. For every $\beta\in\kappa$ there is a unique $j_\beta\in\{0,1\}$ for which $S^{j_\beta}_\beta=\{\alpha\in\lambda:c(\alpha,\beta)=j_\beta\}$ belongs to $\mathscr{W}$.
nodes.statement_short: For each $\beta$ pick the color $j_\beta$ whose column set is in $\mathscr{W}$.

nodes.name: Stabilize the color
nodes.statement: It follows that for some fixed $j$ and a set $B\in\mathscr{U}$ one has $j_\beta=j$ whenever $\beta\in{B}$.
nodes.statement_short: Ultrafilter on $\kappa$ stabilizes $j_\beta=j$ on a set $B\in\mathscr{U}$.

nodes.name: Monochromatic product
nodes.statement: Define $A=\bigcap\{S^j_\beta:\beta\in{B}\}$ and notice that $A\in\mathscr{W}$ by $\lambda$-completeness. Observe that $c''(A\times{B})=\{j\}$, hence we are done proving that $\binom{\lambda}{\kappa}\rightarrow\binom{\mathscr{W}}{\mathscr{U}}$.
nodes.statement_short: $\lambda$-completeness gives $A\in\mathscr{W}$ with $A\times B$ monochromatic.

nodes.name: Coloring from the family
nodes.statement: Assume now that $\{C_\alpha:\alpha\in\lambda\}\subseteq\mathscr{U}$. Define $d:\lambda\times\kappa\rightarrow{2}$ by letting $d(\alpha,\beta)=0$ iff $\beta\in{C_\alpha}$. Let $A\in\mathscr{W},B\in\mathscr{U}$ be such that $d\upharpoonright(A\times{B})$ is constant.
nodes.statement_short: Color $(\alpha,\beta)$ by membership $\beta\in C_\alpha$ and take a monochromatic product.

nodes.name: Constant value is 0
nodes.statement: Notice that the constant value cannot be $1$. Indeed, choose $\alpha\in{A}$ and any element $\beta\in B\cap C_\alpha$ and conclude that $\beta\notin C_\alpha$ if $d''(A\times{B})=\{1\}$, contradicting the choice of $\beta$.
nodes.statement_short: The value 1 is impossible since $B\cap C_\alpha\neq\emptyset$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Thus $d''(A\times{B})=\{0\}$, and hence $B\subseteq\bigcap\{C_\alpha:\alpha\in{A}\}$. Since $B\in\mathscr{U}$, the proof is accomplished.
nodes.statement_short: $B\subseteq\bigcap_{\alpha\in A}C_\alpha$ with $B\in\mathscr{U}$.

nodes.name: Relaxing measurability of $\lambda$
nodes.statement: Let us indicate that in order to obtain the statement ${\rm Gal}(\mathscr{U},\lambda,\lambda)$ from the relevant polarized relation one has to assume that $\kappa$, the domain of $\mathscr{U}$, is measurable, but the assumption that $\lambda$ is also measurable can be relaxed. A moment of perusal shows that if $\binom{\lambda}{\kappa}\rightarrow\binom{\lambda}{\mathscr{U}}$ then ${\rm Gal}(\mathscr{U},\lambda,\lambda)$ obtains. The argument is just the same, and this fact might be helpful.
nodes.statement_short: Only $\kappa$ need be measurable: $\binom{\lambda}{\kappa}\rightarrow\binom{\lambda}{\mathscr{U}}$ already yields ${\rm Gal}(\mathscr{U},\lambda,\lambda)$.

nodes.name: Full Galvin property
nodes.statement: The statement ${\rm Gal}(\mathscr{U},\lambda,\lambda)$ is a strong form of the Galvin property. The above claim establishes a strong Galvin property which will be dubbed as \emph{full}.

nodes.name: Claim 2.1 in ZFC versus AD
nodes.statement: In \textsf{ZFC} this claim is trivial (if $\kappa<\lambda$ and both are measurables) since $\lambda={\rm cf}(\lambda)>2^\kappa$, but without full choice this claim is informative. Under \textsf{AD} it is frequent to meet this strong form, since the distance between regular cardinals and measurable cardinals below $\Theta$ is very small.\footnote{Actually, if $V=L(\mathbb{R})$ then every regular cardinal below $\Theta$ is measurable under \textsf{AD}, see \cite{MR2768698}.}
nodes.statement_short: In ZFC Claim 2.1 is trivial since $\lambda>2^\kappa$; under AD the full Galvin property is common because regular cardinals below $\Theta$ are mostly measurable.

nodes.name: The full Galvin number $\mathfrak{fgp}$
nodes.statement: The full Galvin number. \newline Let $\mathfrak{fgp}$ be the first $\lambda$ for which every family $\mathcal{C}=\{C_\alpha:\alpha\in\lambda^+\}\subseteq\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1}$ contains a subfamily $\mathcal{D}$ of size $\lambda^+$ such that $\bigcap\mathcal{D}\in\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1}$.
differentia: every family $\mathcal{C}=\{C_\alpha:\alpha\in\lambda^+\}\subseteq\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1}$ contains a subfamily $\mathcal{D}$ of size $\lambda^+$ such that $\bigcap\mathcal{D}\in\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1}$
nodes.statement_short: $\mathfrak{fgp}$ is the least $\lambda$ such that every $\lambda^+$ clubs of $\aleph_1$ contain $\lambda^+$ many with club intersection.
nodes.label: deffgp

nodes.name: $\mathsf{AD}$ proves $\mathfrak{fgp}=\aleph_1$
nodes.statement: By Claim \ref{clmmeasurables} and the fact that both $\aleph_1$ and $\aleph_2$ are measurable cardinals under \textsf{AD} we see that $\textsf{AD}\vdash\mathfrak{fgp}=\aleph_1$.
assumptions: both $\aleph_1$ and $\aleph_2$ are measurable cardinals under \textsf{AD}

nodes.name: Consistency strength of ${\rm cf}(\mathfrak{fgp})=\omega$
nodes.statement: The statement ${\rm cf}(\mathfrak{fgp})=\omega$ has some consistency strength.
conclusions: The statement ${\rm cf}(\mathfrak{fgp})=\omega$ has some consistency strength.
nodes.label: propfgpstrength

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.3
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction: a scale with the $\aleph_1$-covering property at $\mu$ turns witnesses below $\mu$ into a witness at $\mu^+$, so $\mathfrak{fgp}\neq\mu$. Good scales (from $\square^*_\mu$) have this property, so ${\rm cf}(\mathfrak{fgp})=\omega$ requires failure of weak squares.

nodes.name: Plan: first step
nodes.statement: The proof consists of two steps. In the first step we show that if $\mu$ is a singular cardinal of countable cofinality, $\mu=\bigcup_{n\in\omega}\mu_n$ where $(\mu_n:n\in\omega)$ is an increasing sequence of regular cardinals, ${\rm tcf}(\prod_{n\in\omega}\mu_n,J^{\rm bd}_\omega)=\mu^+$ and $(f_\alpha:\alpha\in\mu^+)$ is a scale witnessing this fact, endowed with the property that for every $A\in[\mu^+]^{\aleph_1}$ one has $|\{f_\alpha(n):\alpha\in{A}, n\in\omega\}|=\aleph_1$ then $\mathfrak{fgp}\neq\mu$.
nodes.statement_short: Two-step plan; first show a scale with the $\aleph_1$-property forces $\mathfrak{fgp}\neq\mu$.

nodes.name: Assume $\mathfrak{fgp}=\mu$
nodes.statement: By way of contradiction assume that the above assumptions hold yet $\mathfrak{fgp}=\mu$. Thus, for every $n\in\omega$ one has $\mathfrak{fgp}>\mu_n$ and hence one can choose a family $\mathcal{D}_n=\{D^n_\alpha:\alpha\in\mu_n\}\subseteq\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1}$ such that $\bigcap\{D^n_{\alpha_i}:i\in{B}\}$ is bounded in $\omega_1$ whenever $B\in[\mu_n]^{\aleph_1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Assume $\mathfrak{fgp}=\mu$ and choose witnessing families $\mathcal{D}_n$ of size $\mu_n$.

nodes.name: Union family is a witness
nodes.statement: Set $\mathcal{D}=\bigcup\{\mathcal{D}_n:n\in\omega\}$ and notice that $|\mathcal{D}|=\mu$. If $B'\in[\mu]^{\aleph_1}$ then there must be a set $B\in[B']^{\aleph_1}$ and a natural number $n$ such that $B\in[\mu_n]^{\aleph_1}$. One concludes now that: \[|\bigcap\{D^n_{\alpha}:\alpha\in{B'},n\in\omega\}|\leq|\bigcap\{D^n_{\alpha_i}:i\in{B}\}|<\aleph_1\] This is the property that we need with respect to the family $\mathcal{D}$.
nodes.statement_short: The union $\mathcal{D}$ of size $\mu$ has bounded intersections of $\aleph_1$-subfamilies.

nodes.name: Clubs indexed by the scale
nodes.statement: For every $\alpha\in\mu^+$ let $C_\alpha=\bigcap\{D^n_{f_\alpha(n)}:n\in\omega\}$. Observe that $C_\alpha\in\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1}$, being an intersection of but $\aleph_0$ elements of $\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1}$. Let $\mathcal{C}=\{C_\alpha:\alpha\in\mu^+\}$. One can verify that $|\mathcal{C}|=\mu^+$ since $(f_\alpha:\alpha\in\mu^+)$ is a scale.
nodes.statement_short: Define $C_\alpha=\bigcap_n D^n_{f_\alpha(n)}$, giving $\mu^+$ clubs.

nodes.name: Apply $\mathfrak{fgp}=\mu$
nodes.statement: By our assumption, $\mathfrak{fgp}=\mu$. Therefore, one can find $A\in[\mu]^{\aleph_1}$ such that the set $C=\bigcap\{C_\alpha:\alpha\in{A}\}$ belongs to $\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Get $A$ of size $\aleph_1$ with club intersection $C$.

nodes.name: Contradiction
nodes.statement: By our assumptions, $|\{f_\alpha(n):\alpha\in{A}, n\in\omega\}|=\aleph_1$. Let $B=\{f_\alpha(n):\alpha\in{A},n\in\omega\}$, so $B\in[\mu]^{\aleph_1}$. In particular, the set $D=\bigcap\{D^n_{f_\alpha(n)}:\alpha\in{A},n\in\omega\}$ is bounded in $\omega_1$. However, $C=D$ by the above definitions, a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: The scale property makes the same intersection bounded, contradiction.

nodes.name: Second step: good scale
nodes.statement: We proceed now to the second step of the proof. Suppose that $\mu>{\rm cf}(\mu)=\omega$ and there is an increasing sequence $(\mu_n:n\in\omega)$ of regular cardinals such that $\mu=\bigcup_{n\in\omega}\mu_n$ and ${\rm tcf}(\prod_{n\in\omega}\mu_n,J^{\rm bd}_\omega)=\mu^+$. Assume, further, that $(f_\alpha:\alpha\in\mu^+)$ is a \emph{good scale} witnessing this fact.
nodes.statement_short: Second step: assume a good scale on $\prod\mu_n$.

nodes.name: Good scales have the property
nodes.statement: From \cite[Theorem 1.4]{MR4423479} we know that if $A\in[\mu^+]^{\aleph_1}$ then $|\{f_\alpha(n):\alpha\in{A},n\in\omega\}|=\aleph_1$. It follows now from the first step of the proof that $\mathfrak{fgp}\neq\mu$.
nodes.statement_short: Good scales have the $\aleph_1$-property, so the first step gives $\mathfrak{fgp}\neq\mu$.

nodes.name: Weak square gives good scales
nodes.statement: Assume that $\square^*_\mu$ holds at every $\mu\in{2^\omega}$ such that $\mu>{\rm cf}(\mu)=\omega$. It is known that under this assumption, for every such $\mu$ there exists an increasing sequence of regular cardinals $(\mu_n:n\in\omega)$ such that $\mu=\bigcup_{n\in\omega}\mu_n$ and ${\rm tcf}(\prod_{n\in\omega}\mu_n,J^{\rm bd}_\omega)=\mu^+$ and there is a good scale witnessing the latter fact.\footnote{See, e.g. \cite[Section 15]{MR2160657}.} Consequently, $\mathfrak{fgp}\neq\mu$ for every such $\mu$ and hence, in particular, ${\rm cf}(\mathfrak{fgp})>\omega$.
nodes.statement_short: Under $\square^*_\mu$ good scales exist, so ${\rm cf}(\mathfrak{fgp})>\omega$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: It follows that if one wishes to force ${\rm cf}(\mathfrak{fgp})=\omega$ then one must force $\neg\square^*_\mu$ for every $\mu$ of countable cofinality below the continuum, and this setting has some consistency strength, so we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Forcing ${\rm cf}(\mathfrak{fgp})=\omega$ requires failure of weak squares, which has consistency strength.

nodes.name: ${}_\omega{A}$ (countable sups enumeration)
nodes.statement: Let $\kappa$ be a regular and uncountable cardinal. For $A\in[\kappa]^\theta$ let $A_\alpha$ be the $\alpha$th element of $A$ and let ${}_\omega{A}$ be the increasing enumeration of countable sups of elements of $A$, that is $\{\bigcup_{n\in\omega}A_{\alpha+n}:\alpha\in\theta\}$.
nodes.statement_short: For $A\in[\kappa]^\theta$, $A_\alpha$ is its $\alpha$th element and ${}_\omega A$ enumerates sups of its $\omega$-blocks.

nodes.name: $\langle{A}\rangle$
nodes.statement: If $A\in[\kappa]^\kappa$ then let $\langle{A}\rangle$ be the set $\{{}_\omega B:B\in[A]^\kappa\}$.

nodes.name: Magidor-like forcing $\mathbb{M}_{\gamma\kappa}$
nodes.statement: The forcing $\mathbb{M}_{\gamma\kappa}$. \newline Let $\kappa$ be regular and uncountable and assume that $\omega\leq\gamma<\kappa$. \begin{enumerate} \item [$(\aleph)$] A condition $p\in\mathbb{M}_{\gamma\kappa}$ is a pair $(s^p,A^p)$ such that $s^p\in[\kappa]^{<\gamma}, A^p\in[\kappa]^\kappa$ and $\bigcup{s^p}<\bigcap{A^p}$. \item [$(\beth)$] If $p,q\in\mathbb{M}_{\gamma\kappa}$ then $p\leq{q}$ iff $s^p\subseteq{s^q}, \langle{A^q}\rangle\subseteq\langle{A^p}\rangle$ and $s^q-s^p={}_\omega{t}$ for some $t\in[A]^{<\gamma}$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Conditions are pairs (stem of size $<\gamma$, measure-one set of size $\kappa$); extension by inclusion of stems via countable sups.
nodes.label: defmagidorlike

nodes.name: Weak partition cardinal
nodes.statement: We shall say that $\kappa$ is a \emph{weak partition cardinal} if $\kappa\rightarrow(\kappa)^\gamma$ for every $\gamma\in\kappa$.

nodes.name: Henle's theorem on Magidor-like forcing
nodes.statement: Henle proved in \cite{MR722169} that if $\kappa$ is a weak partition cardinal and $\omega<\gamma<\kappa$ then $\mathbb{M}_{\gamma\kappa}$ is a forcing notion which satisfies the Prikry property and preserves cardinals. Moreover, if $G\subseteq\mathbb{M}_{\gamma\kappa}$ is generic then $V[G]$ contains no new bounded subsets of $\kappa$.
assumptions: $\kappa$ is a weak partition cardinal and $\omega<\gamma<\kappa$
conclusions: $\mathbb{M}_{\gamma\kappa}$ is a forcing notion which satisfies the Prikry property and preserves cardinals
$V[G]$ contains no new bounded subsets of $\kappa$

nodes.name: Measurability of $\aleph_1$ preserved
nodes.statement: Let $V$ be a model of $\mathsf{AD}$ and let $G\subseteq\mathbb{M}_{\aleph_1\aleph_2}$ be $V$-generic. Then $\aleph_1$ is measurable in $V[G]$ and $\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1}$ is an ultrafilter.
conclusions: $\aleph_1$ is measurable in $V[G]$ and $\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1}$ is an ultrafilter
nodes.label: clmpreservation

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 2.5
nodes.statement: By a celebrated theorem of Solovay, $\aleph_1$ is measurable in $V$ as witnessed by $\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1}$. Kleinberg proved in \cite{MR0479903} that $\aleph_2$ is a weak partition cardinal under \textsf{AD}. Thus, $\mathbb{M}_{\aleph_1\aleph_2}$ satisfies the above mentioned properties and, in particular, adds no subsets of $\aleph_1$ since any such set is bounded in $\aleph_2$. It follows that $\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1}$ is still a normal ultrafilter over $\aleph_1$ in the generic extension by $\mathbb{M}_{\aleph_1\aleph_2}$, so we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Solovay's measurability of $\aleph_1$ plus Kleinberg's weak partition property of $\aleph_2$ and Henle's theorem: the forcing adds no subsets of $\aleph_1$.

nodes.name: Solovay
nodes.statement: By a celebrated theorem of Solovay, $\aleph_1$ is measurable in $V$ as witnessed by $\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1}$.
nodes.statement_short: By Solovay, $\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1}$ is a measure in $V$.

nodes.name: Kleinberg
nodes.statement: Kleinberg proved in \cite{MR0479903} that $\aleph_2$ is a weak partition cardinal under \textsf{AD}.
nodes.statement_short: By Kleinberg, $\aleph_2$ is a weak partition cardinal under AD.

nodes.name: Apply Henle
nodes.statement: Thus, $\mathbb{M}_{\aleph_1\aleph_2}$ satisfies the above mentioned properties and, in particular, adds no subsets of $\aleph_1$ since any such set is bounded in $\aleph_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Hence the forcing adds no subsets of $\aleph_1$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: It follows that $\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1}$ is still a normal ultrafilter over $\aleph_1$ in the generic extension by $\mathbb{M}_{\aleph_1\aleph_2}$, so we are done.
nodes.statement_short: The club filter remains a normal ultrafilter.

nodes.name: Inclusion rather than end-extension of stems
nodes.statement: Let us indicate that in the definition of the forcing order, $p\leq{q}$ contains the proviso that $s^p\subseteq{s^q}$. We emphasize that the relation here is \emph{inclusion} and not \emph{end-extension} as appears usually in Prikry-type forcing notions. This point plays an important role in some arguments below.

nodes.name: Main Claim: $\aleph_{\omega+1}$ stays regular
nodes.statement: Assume $\mathsf{AD}$ and let $G\subseteq\mathbb{M}_{\aleph_1\aleph_2}$ be $V$-generic. Then $\aleph_{\omega+1}$ is regular in $V[G]$.
nodes.label: mclmpreservation

nodes.name: Proof of Main Claim 3.1
nodes.statement: Recall that ${\rm cf}(\aleph_{\omega+1})^V=\aleph_{\omega+1}>\aleph_2$, since $\aleph_{\omega+1}$ is a measurable cardinal in $V$. Fix a $V$-generic set $G\subseteq\mathbb{M}_{\aleph_1\aleph_2}$. Our goal is to show that ${\rm cf}(\aleph_{\omega+1})^{V[G]}=\aleph_{\omega+1}$ as well. Assume towards contradiction that there is a cardinal $\lambda\in\aleph_{\omega+1}$ and a condition $(a,p)\in\mathbb{M}_{\aleph_1\aleph_2}$ such that $(a,p)\Vdash f:\lambda\rightarrow\aleph_{\omega+1}$, $f$ is order preserving and $\bigcup f''\lambda=\aleph_{\omega+1}$. For every $s\in[p]^{<\omega_1}$ and every $\alpha\in\lambda$ we define the ordinal $\eta_{s\alpha}$ as follows. If there exists $t\in[\omega_2]^{\omega_2}$ such that $(a\cup{}_\omega s,t)\Vdash\mathunderaccent\tilde-3{f}(\alpha)=\check{\beta}$ then $\eta_{s\alpha}=\beta$. If not, let $\eta_{s\alpha}=0$. Notice that $\eta_{s\alpha}$ is well-defined. Indeed, if $t_0,t_1\in[\omega_2]^{\omega_2}$ and $(a\cup{}_\omega s,t_0)\Vdash\mathunderaccent\tilde-3{f}(\alpha)=\check{\beta_0},(a\cup{}_\omega s,t_1)\Vdash\mathunderaccent\tilde-3{f}(\alpha)=\check{\beta_1}$ then necessarily $\beta_0=\beta_1$ since conditions with the same stem are compatible. Now for every $s\in[p]^{<\omega_1}$ let $H_s=\{\eta_{s\alpha}:\alpha\in\lambda\}$, and let $\eta_s=\bigcup H_s$, thus $\eta_s\leq\lambda$. Define a coloring $c:[p]^{<\omega_1}\rightarrow{}^{\omega_1}2$ as follows. Given $s\in[p]^{<\omega_1}$ and $\sigma\in\omega_1$, let $c(s)_\sigma=1$ iff there are $\sigma_0,\sigma_1\in\omega_1$ so that $\sigma<\sigma_0<\sigma_1$ and $\eta_{s\upharpoonright\sigma}<\eta_{s\upharpoonright(\sigma_1-\sigma_0)}$. Recall that $\aleph_2\rightarrow(\aleph_2)^{<\omega_1}$ in $V$, and let $q\in[p]^{\omega_2}$ be $c$-monochromatic. The crucial point here is that for every $\sigma\in\omega_1$ one can find $\sigma'>\sigma, \sigma'\in\omega_1$ and $s'\in[q]^{\sigma'}$ for which $c(s')_{\sigma'}=1$. To see this, fix $\sigma\in\omega_1$ and let $s=q\upharpoonright\sigma$. Pick $r\in[q-s]^{<\omega_1}, t\in[q-s]^{<\omega_2}$ and $\alpha\in\lambda$ such that $(a\cup{}_\omega r,t)\Vdash\mathunderaccent\tilde-3{f}(\alpha)=\beta>\eta_s$. This is possible since $q\subseteq p$ and $(a,p)\Vdash\bigcup f''\lambda=\aleph_{\omega+1}$. Observe that $c(s\cup r)_\sigma=1$ since $\eta_r\geq\beta>\eta_s$. Let $s'=s\cup r$ and let $\sigma'=\ell g(s')$, thus the crucial property holds. Suppose that $s$ is a sequence of \emph{consecutive elements} from $q$ of length $\tau$. We shall say that $s$ is $\tau$-good (or $\tau$-good for $q$), and denote it by $s^g_\tau$. Define $R=\{\eta_{s^g_\tau\alpha}:\alpha\in\lambda,\tau\in\omega_1\}$. Notice that $|R|<\aleph_{\omega+1}$. However, $(a,q)\Vdash f''\lambda\subseteq{R}$, since $q$ is $c$-monochromatic, and hence $f''\lambda$ is bounded in $\aleph_{\omega+1}$. This is a contradiction, so the proof is accomplished.
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction: decide values of a cofinal name via stems, color stems by growth of these values, and use $\aleph_2\rightarrow(\aleph_2)^{<\omega_1}$. A monochromatic set confines the range of $f$ to fewer than $\aleph_{\omega+1}$ values.

nodes.name: Goal
nodes.statement: Recall that ${\rm cf}(\aleph_{\omega+1})^V=\aleph_{\omega+1}>\aleph_2$, since $\aleph_{\omega+1}$ is a measurable cardinal in $V$. Fix a $V$-generic set $G\subseteq\mathbb{M}_{\aleph_1\aleph_2}$. Our goal is to show that ${\rm cf}(\aleph_{\omega+1})^{V[G]}=\aleph_{\omega+1}$ as well.
nodes.statement_short: Fix $G$; show $\aleph_{\omega+1}$ keeps its cofinality.

nodes.name: Assume a short cofinal map
nodes.statement: Assume towards contradiction that there is a cardinal $\lambda\in\aleph_{\omega+1}$ and a condition $(a,p)\in\mathbb{M}_{\aleph_1\aleph_2}$ such that $(a,p)\Vdash f:\lambda\rightarrow\aleph_{\omega+1}$, $f$ is order preserving and $\bigcup f''\lambda=\aleph_{\omega+1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Suppose a condition forces a cofinal order-preserving $f:\lambda\to\aleph_{\omega+1}$.

nodes.name: Decided values $\eta_{s\alpha}$
nodes.statement: For every $s\in[p]^{<\omega_1}$ and every $\alpha\in\lambda$ we define the ordinal $\eta_{s\alpha}$ as follows. If there exists $t\in[\omega_2]^{\omega_2}$ such that $(a\cup{}_\omega s,t)\Vdash\mathunderaccent\tilde-3{f}(\alpha)=\check{\beta}$ then $\eta_{s\alpha}=\beta$. If not, let $\eta_{s\alpha}=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Define $\eta_{s\alpha}$ as the value of $f(\alpha)$ decided by stem $s$.

nodes.name: Well-definedness
nodes.statement: Notice that $\eta_{s\alpha}$ is well-defined. Indeed, if $t_0,t_1\in[\omega_2]^{\omega_2}$ and $(a\cup{}_\omega s,t_0)\Vdash\mathunderaccent\tilde-3{f}(\alpha)=\check{\beta_0},(a\cup{}_\omega s,t_1)\Vdash\mathunderaccent\tilde-3{f}(\alpha)=\check{\beta_1}$ then necessarily $\beta_0=\beta_1$ since conditions with the same stem are compatible.
nodes.statement_short: Conditions with the same stem are compatible.

nodes.name: Sups $\eta_s$
nodes.statement: Now for every $s\in[p]^{<\omega_1}$ let $H_s=\{\eta_{s\alpha}:\alpha\in\lambda\}$, and let $\eta_s=\bigcup H_s$, thus $\eta_s\leq\lambda$.
nodes.statement_short: Let $\eta_s$ be the sup of the values decided by $s$.

nodes.name: Coloring
nodes.statement: Define a coloring $c:[p]^{<\omega_1}\rightarrow{}^{\omega_1}2$ as follows. Given $s\in[p]^{<\omega_1}$ and $\sigma\in\omega_1$, let $c(s)_\sigma=1$ iff there are $\sigma_0,\sigma_1\in\omega_1$ so that $\sigma<\sigma_0<\sigma_1$ and $\eta_{s\upharpoonright\sigma}<\eta_{s\upharpoonright(\sigma_1-\sigma_0)}$.
nodes.statement_short: Color stems by whether the decided values grow.

nodes.name: Partition relation
nodes.statement: Recall that $\aleph_2\rightarrow(\aleph_2)^{<\omega_1}$ in $V$, and let $q\in[p]^{\omega_2}$ be $c$-monochromatic.
nodes.statement_short: Take a $c$-homogeneous $q$ by the partition property of $\aleph_2$.

nodes.name: Crucial property
nodes.statement: The crucial point here is that for every $\sigma\in\omega_1$ one can find $\sigma'>\sigma, \sigma'\in\omega_1$ and $s'\in[q]^{\sigma'}$ for which $c(s')_{\sigma'}=1$. To see this, fix $\sigma\in\omega_1$ and let $s=q\upharpoonright\sigma$. Pick $r\in[q-s]^{<\omega_1}, t\in[q-s]^{<\omega_2}$ and $\alpha\in\lambda$ such that $(a\cup{}_\omega r,t)\Vdash\mathunderaccent\tilde-3{f}(\alpha)=\beta>\eta_s$. This is possible since $q\subseteq p$ and $(a,p)\Vdash\bigcup f''\lambda=\aleph_{\omega+1}$. Observe that $c(s\cup r)_\sigma=1$ since $\eta_r\geq\beta>\eta_s$. Let $s'=s\cup r$ and let $\sigma'=\ell g(s')$, thus the crucial property holds.
nodes.statement_short: For every $\sigma$ some extension of the stem has color 1 at a later coordinate.

nodes.name: Pick an extension
nodes.statement: To see this, fix $\sigma\in\omega_1$ and let $s=q\upharpoonright\sigma$. Pick $r\in[q-s]^{<\omega_1}, t\in[q-s]^{<\omega_2}$ and $\alpha\in\lambda$ such that $(a\cup{}_\omega r,t)\Vdash\mathunderaccent\tilde-3{f}(\alpha)=\beta>\eta_s$. This is possible since $q\subseteq p$ and $(a,p)\Vdash\bigcup f''\lambda=\aleph_{\omega+1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Use cofinality of $f$ to find $r$ deciding a value above $\eta_s$.

nodes.name: Verify the color
nodes.statement: Observe that $c(s\cup r)_\sigma=1$ since $\eta_r\geq\beta>\eta_s$. Let $s'=s\cup r$ and let $\sigma'=\ell g(s')$, thus the crucial property holds.
nodes.statement_short: Then $c(s\cup r)_\sigma=1$.

nodes.name: Good sequences and $R$
nodes.statement: Suppose that $s$ is a sequence of \emph{consecutive elements} from $q$ of length $\tau$. We shall say that $s$ is $\tau$-good (or $\tau$-good for $q$), and denote it by $s^g_\tau$. Define $R=\{\eta_{s^g_\tau\alpha}:\alpha\in\lambda,\tau\in\omega_1\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Define $\tau$-good sequences and the set $R$ of their decided values.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Notice that $|R|<\aleph_{\omega+1}$. However, $(a,q)\Vdash f''\lambda\subseteq{R}$, since $q$ is $c$-monochromatic, and hence $f''\lambda$ is bounded in $\aleph_{\omega+1}$. This is a contradiction, so the proof is accomplished.
nodes.statement_short: $R$ is small but contains the range of $f$, so $f$ is bounded: contradiction.

nodes.name: Negative polarized relation at equal cofinality
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate} \item [$(a)$] If $\kappa={\rm cf}(\lambda)$ then $\binom{\lambda}{\kappa}\nrightarrow\binom{\lambda}{\kappa}$. \item [$(b)$] If ${\rm Gal}(\mathscr{D}_\kappa,\lambda,\lambda)$ holds then $\binom{\lambda}{\kappa}\rightarrow\binom{\lambda}{\kappa}$. \item [$(c)$] If $\kappa={\rm cf}(\lambda)$ then $\neg{\rm Gal}(\mathscr{D}_\kappa,\lambda,\lambda)$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: If $\kappa={\rm cf}(\lambda)$ the polarized relation $\binom{\lambda}{\kappa}\rightarrow\binom{\lambda}{\kappa}$ fails, Galvin implies it, hence ${\rm Gal}(\mathscr{D}_\kappa,\lambda,\lambda)$ fails.
nodes.label: clmsamecof

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 3.2
nodes.statement: We commence with part $(a)$. Fix an increasing and continuous sequence $(\lambda_i:i\in\kappa)$ of ordinals such that $\lambda=\bigcup_{i\in\kappa}\lambda_i$. For every $\alpha\in\lambda$ let $\eta(\alpha)$ be the unique ordinal $i\in\kappa$ so that $\alpha\in[\lambda_i,\lambda_{i+1})$. Define a coloring $c:\lambda\times\kappa\rightarrow{2}$ as follows. Given $\alpha\in\lambda,\beta\in\kappa$ let $c(\alpha,\beta)=0$ iff $\eta(\alpha)\leq\beta$. Suppose that $A\in[\lambda]^\lambda,B\in[\kappa]^\kappa$. Fix $\alpha\in{A}$. Choose $\beta\in{B}$ so that $\eta(\alpha)\leq\beta$. There must be such an ordinal since $B$ is unbounded in $\kappa$. By definition, $c(\alpha,\beta)=0$. Now pick $\alpha'\in{A}$ so that $\eta(\alpha')>\beta$. There must be such an ordinal since $A$ is unbounded in $\lambda$. By definition, $c(\alpha',\beta)=1$. We conclude that $c''(A\times{B})=\{0,1\}$, as required. For part $(b)$, assume that ${\rm Gal}(\mathscr{D}_\kappa,\lambda,\lambda)$ holds and let $c:\lambda\times\kappa\rightarrow{2}$ be any coloring. For every $\alpha\in\lambda$ there is (a unique) $i_\alpha\in\{0,1\}$ such that $S^{i_\alpha}_\alpha=\{\beta\in\kappa:c(\alpha,\beta)=i_\alpha\}\in\mathscr{D}_\kappa$. Fix $A'\in[\lambda]^\lambda,i\in\{0,1\}$ so that $i_\alpha=i$ whenever $\alpha\in{A'}$. Let $\mathcal{D}=\{S^i_\alpha:\alpha\in{A'}$. From ${\rm Gal}(\mathscr{D}_\kappa,\lambda,\lambda)$ we infer that there are $B\in\mathscr{D}_\kappa$ and $A\in[A']^\lambda$ such that $B\subseteq\bigcap\{S^i_\alpha:\alpha\in{A}$. By definition, $c''(A\times{B})=\{i\}$, so we are done proving $(b)$. Finally, part $(c)$ follows from parts $(a)$ and $(b)$.
nodes.statement_short: (a) Color by comparing the cofinal-block index of $\alpha$ with $\beta$; (b) stabilize colors on a club and apply Galvin; (c) combine.

nodes.name: Part (a): the coloring
nodes.statement: We commence with part $(a)$. Fix an increasing and continuous sequence $(\lambda_i:i\in\kappa)$ of ordinals such that $\lambda=\bigcup_{i\in\kappa}\lambda_i$. For every $\alpha\in\lambda$ let $\eta(\alpha)$ be the unique ordinal $i\in\kappa$ so that $\alpha\in[\lambda_i,\lambda_{i+1})$. Define a coloring $c:\lambda\times\kappa\rightarrow{2}$ as follows. Given $\alpha\in\lambda,\beta\in\kappa$ let $c(\alpha,\beta)=0$ iff $\eta(\alpha)\leq\beta$.
nodes.statement_short: Define $c(\alpha,\beta)=0$ iff the block index of $\alpha$ is at most $\beta$.

nodes.name: Color 0 occurs
nodes.statement: Suppose that $A\in[\lambda]^\lambda,B\in[\kappa]^\kappa$. Fix $\alpha\in{A}$. Choose $\beta\in{B}$ so that $\eta(\alpha)\leq\beta$. There must be such an ordinal since $B$ is unbounded in $\kappa$. By definition, $c(\alpha,\beta)=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Unboundedness of $B$ gives a pair of color 0.

nodes.name: Color 1 occurs
nodes.statement: Now pick $\alpha'\in{A}$ so that $\eta(\alpha')>\beta$. There must be such an ordinal since $A$ is unbounded in $\lambda$. By definition, $c(\alpha',\beta)=1$. We conclude that $c''(A\times{B})=\{0,1\}$, as required.
nodes.statement_short: Unboundedness of $A$ gives a pair of color 1, so no product is monochromatic.

nodes.name: Part (b): club rows
nodes.statement: For part $(b)$, assume that ${\rm Gal}(\mathscr{D}_\kappa,\lambda,\lambda)$ holds and let $c:\lambda\times\kappa\rightarrow{2}$ be any coloring. For every $\alpha\in\lambda$ there is (a unique) $i_\alpha\in\{0,1\}$ such that $S^{i_\alpha}_\alpha=\{\beta\in\kappa:c(\alpha,\beta)=i_\alpha\}\in\mathscr{D}_\kappa$. Fix $A'\in[\lambda]^\lambda,i\in\{0,1\}$ so that $i_\alpha=i$ whenever $\alpha\in{A'}$. Let $\mathcal{D}=\{S^i_\alpha:\alpha\in{A'}$.
nodes.statement_short: Each row has a club color class; fix $\lambda$ rows with the same color.

nodes.name: Apply Galvin
nodes.statement: From ${\rm Gal}(\mathscr{D}_\kappa,\lambda,\lambda)$ we infer that there are $B\in\mathscr{D}_\kappa$ and $A\in[A']^\lambda$ such that $B\subseteq\bigcap\{S^i_\alpha:\alpha\in{A}$. By definition, $c''(A\times{B})=\{i\}$, so we are done proving $(b)$.
nodes.statement_short: Galvin yields $A$, $B$ with $A\times B$ monochromatic.

nodes.name: Part (c)
nodes.statement: Finally, part $(c)$ follows from parts $(a)$ and $(b)$.
nodes.statement_short: Combine (a) and (b).

nodes.name: Forcing $\mathfrak{fgp}=\aleph_\omega$ over $\mathsf{AD}$
nodes.statement: One can force over a model of $\mathsf{AD}$ to obtain $\mathfrak{fgp}=\aleph_\omega$.
nodes.label: thmcffgp

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.3
nodes.statement_short: Force with $\mathbb{M}_{\aleph_1\aleph_2}$ over $L(\mathbb{R})$: regularity of $\aleph_{\omega+1}$ and few clubs give $\mathfrak{fgp}\leq\aleph_\omega$. Each $\aleph_n$ ($n\geq2$) gets cofinality $\omega_1$, so Claim 3.2 kills ${\rm Gal}$ below $\aleph_\omega$.

nodes.name: Ground model
nodes.statement: Let $V$ be a model of \textsf{AD}, and assume further that $V=L(\mathbb{R})$. Recall that $\aleph_1, \aleph_2$ and $\aleph_{\omega+1}$ are measurable in $V$, and in particular $\aleph_{\omega+1}$ is regular.
nodes.statement_short: Start from $L(\mathbb{R})\models$ AD where $\aleph_1,\aleph_2,\aleph_{\omega+1}$ are measurable.

nodes.name: Generic extension and preservation
nodes.statement: Let $G\subseteq\mathbb{M}_{\aleph_1\aleph_2}$ be $V$-generic, so $V[G]\models{\rm cf}(\aleph_2)=\omega_1$, thus $V[G]$ is not a model of \textsf{AD}. However, $\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1}$ is still a normal ultrafilter in $V[G]$ by virtue of Claim \ref{clmpreservation}. Likewise, $V[G]\models\aleph_{\omega+1}$ is a regular cardinal due to the main claim.
nodes.statement_short: Force with $\mathbb{M}_{\aleph_1\aleph_2}$; the club filter stays an ultrafilter and $\aleph_{\omega+1}$ stays regular.

nodes.name: Few clubs
nodes.statement: Suppose that $\langle A_\alpha:\alpha\in\aleph_{\omega+1}\rangle$ is a sequence of elements of $\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1}$ in $V[G]$. Since $V[G]$ contains no new subsets of $\aleph_1$ one concludes from \cite[Theorem 8.26]{MR2768698} that $|\{A_\alpha:\alpha\in\aleph_{\omega+1}\}|\leq\aleph_1$.
nodes.statement_short: Only $\aleph_1$ many distinct clubs appear in the sequence.

nodes.name: Upper bound
nodes.statement: Since $\aleph_{\omega+1}$ is regular in $V[G]$, there are $T\in[\aleph_{\omega+1}]^{\aleph_{\omega+1}}$ and $A\in\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1}$ such that $\alpha\in{T}\Rightarrow A_\alpha=A$. This fact witnesses ${\rm Gal}(\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1},\aleph_{\omega+1},\aleph_{\omega+1})$ and hence $\mathfrak{fgp}\leq\aleph_\omega$ in $V[G]$.
nodes.statement_short: Regularity gives $\aleph_{\omega+1}$ equal clubs, so $\mathfrak{fgp}\leq\aleph_\omega$.

nodes.name: Reduce lower bound
nodes.statement: Trivially, $\mathfrak{fgp}\geq\aleph_1$, e.g. by the collection of end-segments of $\aleph_1$. So let us prove that if $0<n<\omega$ then $\mathfrak{fgp}\neq\aleph_n$. In other words, let us show that $\neg{\rm Gal}(\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1},\aleph_{n+1},\aleph_{n+1})$ whenever $n<\omega$.
nodes.statement_short: It remains to refute ${\rm Gal}(\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1},\aleph_{n+1},\aleph_{n+1})$.

nodes.name: Cofinalities in $V[G]$
nodes.statement: Recall that ${\rm cf}(\aleph_n)=\omega_2$ under \textsf{AD} for every $n\in[2,\omega)$. Hence in $V[G]$ one has ${\rm cf}(\aleph_n)=\omega_1$ for every $n\in[2,\omega)$. Similarly, ${\rm cf}(\aleph_1)=\aleph_1$ in $V[G]$, since $\aleph_1$ is measurable and hence regular.
nodes.statement_short: In $V[G]$ each $\aleph_n$, $n\geq2$, has cofinality $\omega_1$.

nodes.name: Apply Claim 3.2
nodes.statement_short: Claim 3.2 gives failure of the Galvin property at each $\aleph_{n+1}$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Therefore, $\mathfrak{fgp}\geq\aleph_\omega$ and then $\mathfrak{fgp}=\aleph_\omega$ as required.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathfrak{fgp}=\aleph_\omega$.

nodes.name: $\mathfrak{fgp}$ after Prikry forcing into $\aleph_2$
nodes.statement: It is possible, of course, to force Prikry into $\aleph_2$, and then the cofinality of every $\aleph_n$ above $\aleph_1$ will be countable. However, we do not know whether $\mathfrak{fgp}=\aleph_\omega$ in this model.

nodes.name: Independence of singular polarized relations
nodes.statement: Polarized relations of the form $\binom{\mu}{\kappa}\rightarrow\binom{\mu}{\kappa}$ where $\kappa={\rm cf}(\kappa)>\mu$ and $\mu>{\rm cf}(\mu)$ were studied in \cite{MR0202613}. The authors were interested, inter alia, in the situation in which $\kappa={\rm cf}(\mu)^+$. It is shown in \cite{MR4101445} that such relations are independent.

nodes.name: Lévy-Solovay theorem
nodes.statement: A celebrated theorem of L\'evy and Solovay from \cite{MR224458} says that if $\kappa$ is measurable and $\mathbb{P}$ is a forcing notion of size less than $\kappa$ then $\kappa$ remains measurable in any generic extension by $\mathbb{P}$.
assumptions: $\mathbb{P}$ is a forcing notion of size less than $\kappa$
conclusions: $\kappa$ remains measurable in any generic extension by $\mathbb{P}$

nodes.name: Preservation of measurability of $\aleph_{\omega+1}$
nodes.statement: Nonetheless, it seems reasonable to assume that the measurability of $\aleph_{\omega+1}$ will be preserved if one forces with $\mathbb{M}_{\aleph_1\aleph_2}$ over a model of \textsf{AD}.
assumptions: one forces with $\mathbb{M}_{\aleph_1\aleph_2}$ over a model of \textsf{AD}
conclusions: the measurability of $\aleph_{\omega+1}$ will be preserved

nodes.name: Henle: Prikry forcing into $\aleph_1$ preserves measurability of $\aleph_2$
nodes.statement: We indicate that if one forces with Prikry forcing into $\aleph_1$ over a model of \textsf{AD} then $\aleph_2$ remains measurable in the generic extension,\footnote{This is a result of Henle, see \cite[Proposition 3.5]{MR722169}.} so the parallel situation with respect to $\aleph_{\omega_1}$ is plausible.
assumptions: one forces with Prikry forcing into $\aleph_1$ over a model of \textsf{AD}
conclusions: $\aleph_2$ remains measurable in the generic extension

nodes.name: Alternative route via measurability of $\aleph_{\omega+1}$
nodes.statement: If, however, $\aleph_{\omega+1}$ remains measurable, then $\binom{\aleph_{\omega+1}}{\aleph_1}\rightarrow\binom{\mathscr{W}}{\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1}}$, where $\mathscr{W}$ is a normal ultrafilter over $\aleph_{\omega+1}$, as proved in Claim \ref{clmmeasurables}. From this one concludes that ${\rm Gal}(\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1},\aleph_{\omega+1},\aleph_{\omega+1})$ holds and hence $\mathfrak{fgp}\leq\aleph_\omega$ in $V[G]$. The opposite direction is proved exactly as in the proof of the above theorem.
nodes.statement_short: If $\aleph_{\omega+1}$ stays measurable, Claim 2.1's polarized relation gives the Galvin property and $\mathfrak{fgp}\leq\aleph_\omega$; the lower bound is as in Theorem 3.3.

nodes.name: Question 3.4 (measurability after $\mathbb{M}_{\aleph_1\aleph_2}$)
nodes.statement: Let $V$ be a model of \textsf{AD}, and let $G$ be $V$-generic for $\mathbb{M}_{\aleph_1\aleph_2}$. \begin{enumerate} \item [$(\aleph)$] Is $\aleph_{\omega+1}$ a measurable cardinal in $V[G]$? \item [$(\beth)$] Is the collection of $\omega$-closed unbounded subsets of $\aleph_{\omega+1}$ a normal ultrafilter in $V[G]$? \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: qmeasurability

nodes.name: Larger values of $\mathfrak{gp}$ with countable cofinality
nodes.statement: Let us observe that the value of $\mathfrak{gp}$ is not confined to $\aleph_\omega$ using this method. That is, one can force ${\rm cf}(\mathfrak{gp})=\omega$ with larger values of $\mathfrak{gp}$. For example, one can start with $\mathbb{M}_{\aleph_1\kappa}$ where $\kappa=\aleph_{\omega+2}$ followed by the same forcing notion where $\kappa=\aleph_{\omega+1}$. Since Magidor forcing in this context adds no bounded subsets to $\kappa$, $\aleph_{\omega+1}$ remains measurable after the first step, and hence one can perform the second step. Finally, one should force with $\mathbb{M}_{\aleph_1\aleph_2}$, using again the fact that $\aleph_2$ will remain measurable after the first two steps of the iteration. In the resulting model, all the cardinals up to $\aleph_{\omega^{\omega^\omega}+1}$ are either of countable cofinality or of cofinality $\aleph_1$. On the other hand, $\aleph_{\omega^{\omega^\omega}+1}$ remains a regular cardinal, by the arguments of Main Claim \ref{mclmpreservation}. Thus, $\mathfrak{gp}=\aleph_{\omega^{\omega^\omega}+1}$ in the generic extension.
nodes.statement_short: Iterating Magidor-like forcings at $\aleph_{\omega+2}$, $\aleph_{\omega+1}$, $\aleph_2$ yields larger values of the Galvin number.

nodes.name: A witness family of size $\mu$ when ${\rm cf}(\mu)=\omega$
nodes.statement: Fix $\mu>{\rm cf}(\mu)=\omega$. If $\mathfrak{gp}=\mu$ then there is a family $\mathcal{D}=\{D_\alpha:\alpha\in\mu\}\subseteq\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1}$ such that $\bigcap\{D_\alpha:\alpha\in{B}\}$ is not in $\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1}$ whenever $B\in[\mu]^{\aleph_1}$.
nodes.section: Remarks on the Galvin number in ZFC
conclusions: there is a family $\mathcal{D}=\{D_\alpha:\alpha\in\mu\}\subseteq\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1}$ such that $\bigcap\{D_\alpha:\alpha\in{B}\}$ is not in $\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1}$ whenever $B\in[\mu]^{\aleph_1}$

nodes.name: Argument for the countable-cofinality witness
nodes.statement: Indeed, choose an increasing sequence $(\mu_n:n\in\omega)$ of regular cardinals such that $\mu=\bigcup_{n\in\omega}\mu_n$. For every $n\in\omega$ we are assuming that $\mathfrak{gp}>\mu_n$. Hence there is a family $\mathcal{D}_n=\{D^n_\alpha:\alpha\in\mu_n^+\}$ witnessing this fact. Let $\mathcal{D}=\bigcup_{n\in\omega}\mathcal{D}_n$. Now if $B\in[\mu]^{\aleph_1}$ then there are $n\in\omega$ and $C\in[B]^{\aleph_1}$ so that $C\in[\mu_n^+]^{\aleph_1}$. It follows that $D=\bigcap\{D_\alpha:\alpha\in{C}\}$ is not in $\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1}$ by the choice of $\mathcal{D}_n$.
nodes.section: Remarks on the Galvin number in ZFC
nodes.statement_short: Union of witnesses below each $\mu_n$; any $\aleph_1$-subset of $\mu$ has an $\aleph_1$-subset inside some $\mu_n^+$.

nodes.name: Witnesses below $\mu$
nodes.statement: Indeed, choose an increasing sequence $(\mu_n:n\in\omega)$ of regular cardinals such that $\mu=\bigcup_{n\in\omega}\mu_n$. For every $n\in\omega$ we are assuming that $\mathfrak{gp}>\mu_n$. Hence there is a family $\mathcal{D}_n=\{D^n_\alpha:\alpha\in\mu_n^+\}$ witnessing this fact.
nodes.section: Remarks on the Galvin number in ZFC
nodes.statement_short: Pick witness families $\mathcal{D}_n$ at each $\mu_n^+$.

nodes.name: Union works
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{D}=\bigcup_{n\in\omega}\mathcal{D}_n$. Now if $B\in[\mu]^{\aleph_1}$ then there are $n\in\omega$ and $C\in[B]^{\aleph_1}$ so that $C\in[\mu_n^+]^{\aleph_1}$. It follows that $D=\bigcap\{D_\alpha:\alpha\in{C}\}$ is not in $\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1}$ by the choice of $\mathcal{D}_n$.
nodes.section: Remarks on the Galvin number in ZFC
nodes.statement_short: Any $\aleph_1$-subset concentrates on some $\mu_n^+$, as cofinality is countable.

nodes.name: The argument fails for cofinality $\omega_1$
nodes.statement: This argument breaks down if $\mu>{\rm cf}(\mu)=\omega_1$. One can choose a sequence $(\mu_i:i\in\omega_1)$ and $\mathcal{D}_i$ for every $i\in\omega_1$ as before. But now it is possible that $B\in[\mu]^{\aleph_1}$ while $|B\cap\mu_i|<\aleph_1$ for each $i\in\omega_1$. Therefore, the argument for the consistency strength of the statement ${\rm cf}(\mathfrak{gp})=\omega_1$ is false.
nodes.section: Remarks on the Galvin number in ZFC
nodes.statement_short: For ${\rm cf}(\mu)=\omega_1$ an $\aleph_1$-set can meet each $\mu_i$ in a countable set, so the consistency-strength argument of MR4423479 for ${\rm cf}(\mathfrak{gp})=\omega_1$ fails.

nodes.name: Ultimate failure of the Galvin property
nodes.statement: Suppose that $\mathcal{C}=\{C_\alpha:\alpha\in\lambda\}\subseteq\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1}$ witnesses the failure of the Galvin property. We shall say that $\mathcal{C}$ witnesses the \emph{ultimate failure of the Galvin property} if $\lambda=2^{\omega_1}$.
nodes.section: Remarks on the Galvin number in ZFC
nodes.definiendum: ultimate failure of the Galvin property

nodes.name: Ultimate failure forces cofinality above $\omega_1$
nodes.statement: If ${\rm cf}(\lambda)=\omega_1$ then $2^{\omega_1}\neq\lambda$, so if $\mathfrak{gp}=\mu$ exemplifies the ultimate failure of Galvin's property then ${\rm cf}(\mu)>\omega_1$.
nodes.section: Remarks on the Galvin number in ZFC
assumptions: $\mathfrak{gp}=\mu$ exemplifies the ultimate failure of Galvin's property

nodes.name: Forcing $\mathfrak{gp}=\lambda$ with ${\rm cf}(\lambda)=\omega_1$
nodes.statement: Assume $\mathsf{GCH}$. One can force $\mathfrak{gp}=\lambda$ whenever $\lambda>{\rm cf}(\lambda)=\omega_1$. Moreover, this statement has no consistency strength.
nodes.section: Remarks on the Galvin number in ZFC
conclusions: this statement has no consistency strength
nodes.label: clmcorrect

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 4.1
nodes.statement: Let $\bar{\mathbb{S}}=\prod_{\alpha\in\lambda}\mathbb{S}_\alpha$ be the forcing notion of Abraham and Shelah from \cite{MR830084}. Each component $\mathbb{S}_\alpha$ is a tow-step iteration in which the first step adds a Cohen real and the second step adds a club to $\aleph_1$. For us it is important to observe that $\bar{\mathbb{S}}$ adds $\lambda$-many Cohen reals. Let $G\subseteq\bar{\mathbb{S}}$ be $V$-generic. In $V[G]$ one has a family $\mathcal{C}=\{C_\alpha:\alpha\in\lambda\}$ which witnesses the failure of the Galvin property. Notice that ${\rm cf}(\lambda)>\omega_1$ is required in \cite{MR830084} only for the purpose of the ultimate failure, that is $2^{\omega_1}=\lambda$. This point is elaborated in \cite{MR4611828}. In our case, the family $\mathcal{C}$ is not a witness for the ultimate failure since $2^{\omega_1}>\lambda$ in $V[G]$ because ${\rm cf}(\lambda)=\omega_1$. However, $2^\omega=\lambda$ in $V[G]$ since $\bar{\mathbb{S}}$ adds only $\lambda$-many Cohen reals and $\lambda^\omega=\lambda$ in the ground model. Thus, we know that $\mathfrak{gp}\geq\lambda$ by the above forcing. But we also have the cardinal arithmetic constellation of $2^\omega=\lambda<2^{\omega_1}$ and hence ${\rm Gal}(\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1},\aleph_1,\lambda^+)$ holds as proved in \cite{MR3604115}. Therefore, $\mathfrak{gp}=\lambda$ as required.
nodes.section: Remarks on the Galvin number in ZFC
nodes.statement_short: Use the Abraham-Shelah product with ${\rm cf}(\lambda)=\omega_1$: it gives $\mathfrak{gp}\geq\lambda$ and $2^\omega=\lambda<2^{\omega_1}$, so the Galvin property at $\lambda^+$ gives $\mathfrak{gp}=\lambda$.

Each component $\mathbb{S}_\alpha$ is a tow-step iteration in which the first step adds a Cohen real and the second step adds a club to $\aleph_1$. For us it is important to observe that $\bar{\mathbb{S}}$ adds $\lambda$-many Cohen reals.

nodes.name: Failure witness

nodes.statement_short: Cofinality $\omega_1$ only affects the ultimate failure; here $2^{\omega_1}>\lambda$.

nodes.name: Continuum is $\lambda$
nodes.statement: However, $2^\omega=\lambda$ in $V[G]$ since $\bar{\mathbb{S}}$ adds only $\lambda$-many Cohen reals and $\lambda^\omega=\lambda$ in the ground model.

nodes.name: Galvin at $\lambda^+$
nodes.statement: Thus, we know that $\mathfrak{gp}\geq\lambda$ by the above forcing. But we also have the cardinal arithmetic constellation of $2^\omega=\lambda<2^{\omega_1}$ and hence ${\rm Gal}(\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1},\aleph_1,\lambda^+)$ holds as proved in \cite{MR3604115}.
nodes.section: Remarks on the Galvin number in ZFC
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound from the witness; Galvin at $\lambda^+$ from $2^\omega=\lambda$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Therefore, $\mathfrak{gp}=\lambda$ as required.
nodes.section: Remarks on the Galvin number in ZFC
nodes.statement_short: $\mathfrak{gp}=\lambda$.

nodes.name: The Abraham-Shelah forcing at countable cofinality
nodes.statement: One can force with \cite{MR830084} where $\lambda>{\rm cf}(\lambda)=\omega$ as well. The same argument will show that $\mathfrak{gp}\geq\lambda$. However, $2^\omega>\lambda$ in this case, so one cannot prove that $\mathfrak{gp}=\lambda$. In fact, it seems that one can define explicitly a family of size $\lambda^+$, witnessing the failure of the Galvin property in this model.
nodes.section: Remarks on the Galvin number in ZFC
nodes.statement_short: For ${\rm cf}(\lambda)=\omega$ the same forcing gives $\mathfrak{gp}\geq\lambda$, but $2^\omega>\lambda$ blocks the upper bound.

nodes.name: Alouf's question
nodes.statement: Is it consistent that $\mu>{\rm cf}(\mu)=\omega_1, \mathfrak{gp}=\mu$ and yet every $\mathcal{D}\in[\mathscr{D}_{\aleph_1}]^\mu$ satisfies the Galvin property?

nodes.name: Cardinal arithmetic when ${\rm cf}(\mathfrak{gp})=\omega$
nodes.statement: Suppose that $\mu>{\rm cf}(\mu)=\omega$ and $\mathfrak{gp}=\mu$. Then $2^\theta=\mu^+$ for every $\aleph_0\leq\theta\leq\mu$.
nodes.section: Remarks on the Galvin number in ZFC
nodes.label: rcountablecof

nodes.name: Proof of Remark 4.3
nodes.statement: By a result of Shelah, if $2^\mu>\mu^+$ then there is a good scale at $\mu^+$, see \cite{MR1318912} or \cite[Section 19]{MR2160657}. Thus, if $\mathfrak{gp}=\mu$ then necessarily $2^\mu=\mu^+$. Likewise, if $2^{\aleph_0}<\mu$ then $\mathfrak{gp}\leq 2^{\aleph_0}<\mu$. Hence, if $\mathfrak{gp}=\mu$ then $2^{\aleph_0}\geq\mu$ and then necessarily $2^{\aleph_0}\geq\mu^+$. Since $2^{\aleph_0}\leq 2^\mu=\mu^+$, we are done.
nodes.section: Remarks on the Galvin number in ZFC
nodes.statement_short: Shelah's good scale theorem forces $2^\mu=\mu^+$, and $\mathfrak{gp}\leq 2^{\aleph_0}$ forces $2^{\aleph_0}\geq\mu^+$; squeeze.
